name: Ruins of Eldarath
summary: Naga overrun the Ruins of Eldarath along Azshara’s rocky bluffs. Once a Highborne city of arcane study, its surviving plazas and temples still draw scholars and adventurers seeking ancient tablets and relics.

sections.title: A Shattered Highborne Bastion
sections.body:
Before the Great Sundering shattered Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Eldarath flourished as a night elven city. Highborne mages gathered there and carved their deepest arcane insights and fundamental magical rules into grand stone tablets.

They left the tablets in public squares for their peers to study. The Sundering sank much of the city into the Bay of Storms. Modern night elves have shunned the surviving ruins along the eastern cliffs for millennia, while salt spray and ivy slowly claim them.

sections.title: Naga Rule and Forgotten Relics
sections.body:
Vicious naga have risen from the sea and seized Eldarath’s shattered streets. Warlords command them from nearby sanctuaries, including the Temple of Zin-Malor. Yet danger has not kept outsiders away.

The Explorers' League sends Alliance adventurers into the broken courtyards to take rubbings of the ancient tablets. Whispers of lost treasures and lingering magic have also drawn the blue dragon Azuregos to the surrounding wilderness. Beneath the cracked flagstones, secrets of immense power may still lie buried.

faq.q: What was Eldarath before it fell into ruins?
faq.answer: Before the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago, Eldarath flourished as a night elven city populated by the Highborne. It was a center of arcane study and a fortified haven until the Sundering devastated it.

faq.q: Who controls the Ruins of Eldarath today?
faq.answer: Hostile naga now overrun the ruins and hold the crumbling plazas and nearby structures as coastal strongholds. Warlords such as Krellian command them from places like the Temple of Zin-Malor.

faq.q: Why do scholars and explorers travel to Eldarath?
faq.answer: Scholars seek the ancient stone tablets left by Highborne mages. The public tablets record fundamental rules of arcane magic and long-lost research. Groups such as the Dwarven Explorers' League send scouts to secure rubbings.

faq.q: Why is the blue dragon Azuregos roaming near the ruins?
faq.answer: Azuregos is drawn to the ancient arcane power lingering along Azshara’s coast. Rumors say powerful relics from before the Sundering may remain hidden in or around the ruins, perhaps even vials touched by the ancient Well of Eternity.

angles.text: As a mage, you find a solemn place of study in Eldarath. Tablets across its plazas preserve foundational arcane theories carved by gifted Highborne sorcerers before their empire fell.
As a night elf, you see the Highborne’s hubris and the Sundering in these sun-bleached ruins. Modern Kaldorei long avoided them, and naga now defile the ruins.
